summary: Fix dropped-subject re-entrancy rule, restrict habitual, fronted 为了 -> have-reason-91, no nodes for additive 还/也/甚至, add 靠/有能力/如/全/V到/-00/patient 人 constructions, ban :poss, temporal fixes (chained conjuncts, reported past, participles, evaluative statements), modal conjunct conceiver and headline complement; trim redundancies for space.

edits.old:
The same holds for dropped subjects and objects of finite clauses (in coordination, contrast or a chain of clauses): do not
  add a re-entrancy to an earlier mention; leave the argument out. This also holds for infinitive-like and
  trailing clauses (never fill their agent with an entity of the main clause) and for possessors: a word like 旗下 is a `:mod`
  concept, not a `:possessor` taken from elsewhere.
edits.new: But a dropped subject shared by coordinated clauses or a chain of actions of the same agent re-enters (as the role its roleset gives, usually `:ARG0`) in every conjunct; the main subject also re-enters as agent of a 为了 purpose clause and of the complement of an ability or control word. Dropped objects are left out, and a word like 旗下 is a `:mod` concept, not a `:possessor` taken from elsewhere.

edits.old:
This holds whatever the tense, and also under an
   aspectual verb (continue, stop).
edits.new: Only a generic practice is habitual: one publishing/reporting act on a specific counted item (一篇), with 了, or tied to an occasion is `performance`. A purpose event in a past narrative takes the main event's aspect.

edits.anchor:
nesting have-purpose-91 inside have-reason-91
  when both occur.
edits.text: A fronted 为了 clause with no paired marker: gold uses `have-reason-91 :ARG1 <main event> :ARG2 <purpose event>` (confirm with `search_annotations`).

edits.old: - Every adverb that carries meaning (*already, still, also, all/both*; 已经, 仍, 也, 都, 均) gets its own node,
edits.new: - Every adverb with real scope (*already, still, all/both*; 已经, 仍, 都, 均) gets its own node (甚至 and additive 还/也 that only link a clause to the previous clause or sentence get none),

edits.new:

e.g. founding); a verb + 人 naming the patient (a V-ed person) is `(r / 人 :ARG1-of (v / verb-01 :aspect process))`.

edits.anchor: - Change verbs with 由 X 改为/变为 Y: the original X is `:ARG1` and the result Y is `:ARG2`; never `:source`.
edits.text:
- Never `:poss` (not a role): content/section of a publication → `:part-of`; staff of an organisation, a country's policy → `:possessor`; the domain of a policy/problem noun → `:topic`.
- 靠/通过 X (实现) Y: X's event is `:reason` of Y, no node for 靠/通过. 有能力 V: `(y / 有-06 :ARG0 S :ARG1 (n / 能力 :ARG1-of (i / identity-91 :ARG2 (v / V-01 :ARG0 S) :aspect state)))`, modal `(author :full-affirmative i)` `(author :neutral-affirmative v)`. Sentence-initial 如 (for example) → `(h / have-example-91 :ARG1 (implicit-predicate) :ARG2 <main event>)`. 全 + noun → noun `:mod 全`. V+到/在/上: if PropBank lists the compound, use it and read its role glosses. A roleset with no usable roles → `-00`.

edits.old: a sentence about the current state (with currently/already, 目前/已经, or a present naming or labelling verb).
edits.new: a sentence about the current state (with currently/already, 目前/已经, or a present naming or labelling verb). A general evaluation of a subject narrated in the past, with no present marker, is `:before`.

edits.old: Clauses restating or qualifying a report's content take the content's main event as parent, not the reporting verb.
edits.new: Clauses restating or qualifying a report's content take the content's main event as parent, not the reporting verb. A reported event earlier than the report is `(report :before content)`; a date inside reported content gets no temporal parent and parents no event.

edits.old:
- A relative-clause or participle event that describes an earlier completed event (left over, inherited, built) is before the
  event whose argument it modifies: `(main :before rc-event)`.
edits.new: - A relative-clause or participle event is `(main :before rc-event)` only when anteriority is explicit (left over, inherited); otherwise an attributive participle `:overlap`s.

edits.old: every reporting or claiming verb with that speaker as subject (each verb of a series of reports too) gets `(src :full-affirmative verb)`
edits.new: every verb with that speaker as subject in the same coordination (reports and other acts) gets `(src :full-affirmative verb)`

edits.text: The nested complement (serve as X) of a want/support verb in a quoted headline gets no `:quote`, aspect or links.
